Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)  
- Assessment based on transcript and DDx:  
  - High likelihood of irritant contact dermatitis due to occupational exposure to cleaning products without consistent glove use, with symptoms onset correlating with recent job change.  
  - Secondary consideration of diabetic xerosis contributing to skin dryness given known type 2 diabetes, although symptoms worsened with chemical exposure suggesting irritant predominance.  
  - Allergic contact dermatitis possible but less likely—no personal/family history of allergies or classic allergic features; antihistamines ineffective.  
  - Other diagnoses such as fungal infection and psoriasis considered unlikely given clinical picture and history; no supporting features detected.  
- No contradictions noted between transcript and DDx findings.  

Management Plan  
- Strong advice to wear protective gloves consistently during cleaning to avoid further irritant exposure  
- Prescribe topical corticosteroids (unspecified dose/route/frequency) to reduce inflammation  
- Recommend frequent use of stronger emollients (3-4 times daily) to restore skin barrier and hydration for at least 2 weeks  
- Review advised in 1-2 weeks to assess response; earlier review if worsening symptoms or spreading  
- Prescription to be sent electronically to pharmacy  
- Patient education regarding trigger avoidance and symptom monitoring

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):  
- Irritant contact dermatitis (High likelihood): Supported by direct occupational chemical exposure without gloves, symptom onset after job change, localized symptoms on the hands.  
- Diabetic xerosis with possible secondary changes (Moderate likelihood): Known diabetes with associated dry skin that may contribute to severity; skin symptoms worsened by irritants.  
- Allergic contact dermatitis (Moderate likelihood): Possible immune-mediated reaction to work chemicals; lacks classic rash and did not respond to antihistamines, making it less likely but still considered.
